evidence: The whole-product delta retains the v0.4.x Codex and Claude whole-plugin paths and their exact provider/runtime security controls from the unpublished v0.4.1/v0.4.2 candidates; exact PR-candidate Codex/Claude rehearsal remains required before merge.

Accepted-main staging now exercises Codex whole-plugin MCP initialize/tools-list/tool-call plus post-runtime clean closure against the exact future shipping archive, while Claude stage evidence uses the same exact archive in a genuine local selected-plugin TTY before tag.

gate_contract regression coverage now requires PRETAG staged-byte runtime closure, forbids full CI on v* tags, requires promotion-only tag automation, and forbids post-tag provider/latest/runtime evidence paths.

check-post-tag-surface.py scans the tag-triggered workflow and pre-publish verifier fail-closed for build/test/provider/runtime/registry-latest/repository-admin blockers and rejects any non-release workflow that reintroduces a v* tag trigger.
Accepted-main staging rehearses the exact Actions artifact-read capability later used for promotion with the same workflow-scoped token permission before any protected tag exists.
Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock advance only the clean-room-launcher package version from the unpublished 0.4.2 candidate to 0.4.3; no Rust runtime/build dependency is added, removed or replaced.

Provider qualification remains pinned to Codex 0.156.0 and Claude Code 2.1.280 with canonical npm package/platform integrity. Registry freshness is checked while staging, then frozen into the accepted stage manifest instead of being re-decided after tag.

Release candidate readiness on accepted main now produces a content-addressed release-stage artifact for the exact accepted SHA and a separate pre-tag attestation rehearsal proves the actions/attestation mechanism and workflow-token artifact-read capability.
The ordinary CI workflow no longer triggers on v* tags, eliminating a second full test graph after the irreversible tag boundary.

The tag-triggered Release workflow contains no cargo build/test/fetch, provider provisioning/qualification/runtime, npm latest/package, or repository-admin policy check; it resolves and promotes only a successful exact accepted-main stage.

PRETAG_BLOCKER_CLOSURE is implemented as exact accepted-main staging: shipping archive/SBOM/checksums/release notes/provider tuple and runtime evidence are bound in clroom.release-stage.v1 before tag.

push-release-tag.sh requires the exact successful accepted-main stage plus local Claude exact-stage TTY evidence, verifies tag/Release absence, no-bypass tag protection and Immutable Releases with the Owner-authenticated gh session, then performs one protected tag push after a final mutable-state refresh.

release.yml is promotion-only: it resolves the preaccepted stage, creates unavoidable tag-bound provenance/SBOM attestations, uploads exactly those bytes to a guarded Draft and downloads/cmp-reconciles the six remote assets.

verify-draft-release.sh compares Draft payload bytes to the accepted stage and validates tag-bound attestations and Immutable Releases without rebuilding, rerunning Codex/Claude or asking npm whether the frozen provider tuple is still latest.

Transient GitHub transport failures after tag are reconciliation/retry events on the same immutable tag; a deterministic blocker first observable post-tag is now classified as a harness escape rather than consuming another release number.
Active README, SECURITY and provider/support documentation identify v0.4.3 as the current source contract while v0.4.1 and v0.4.2 remain explicitly unpublished historical candidates.
CHANGELOG v0.4.3 documents the release-harness incident and the pre-tag staged-byte architecture without claiming that v0.4.1 or v0.4.2 were published.
The existing public documentation version-coherence gate continues to bind current provider claims to Codex 0.156.0 / Claude Code 2.1.280 and rejects stale current-product version claims.

near_misses.durable_control: Codex activation requires both exact-bundle projection into the active private shadow PluginStore and session-layer exact plugin enablement; session flags alone are not treated as qualification evidence.

Shadow PluginStore selection is single-bundle only, verified by path+digest ownership marker and cache-only-selected checks; stale owned projections are reconciled, while unknown siblings or tampered projections fail closed and are preserved rather than blindly deleted.

Projection preserves executable bits while removing write bits recursively; provider sandbox also write-denies the shadow plugin cache and marker, with regression tests for read-only and executable semantics.
Provider identity/version, installed source identity/digest and projected bundle are revalidated after planning and again immediately before provider exec; any drift refuses before provider birth.
When CLROOM plugin selection is active, raw Codex config/profile/feature/plugin controls are refused before provider birth; arguments after the provider terminator remain literal.

Canonical provider-pins.sh records exact current-stable versions and npm integrity; check-provider-pins.sh verifies latest tags and integrity during candidate provisioning and again at the action-time tag boundary.

Release contract tests and qualification evidence verification consume the canonical pinned provider versions instead of duplicating stale provider version/digest literals; evidence is rejected unless its provider version exactly matches the pinned canary version.
Public identity tests include features.remote_plugin=false in the exact Codex clean argv contract while preserving native Codex process identity and passthrough semantics.
The post-v0.4.0 release delta explicitly verifies the exported SBOM attestation bundle with the CycloneDX predicate before publication.

Protected-tag helper refreshes main/tag/ruleset/release-contract/provider-pin state at action time, compares local provider version and bytes to pretag evidence, performs one tag push, then reconciles the authoritative remote result.

Release readiness provisions the pinned current Codex canary before full locked tests; negative qualification tests derive the executable's actual provider version and therefore exercise the fail-closed harness instead of returning early or failing before evidence creation.

Codex v0.4.1 uses a new .clroom-clean-state-v2/.clroom-state-v2 shadow generation. Legacy v1 shadow state is preserved but never imported or deleted; regression coverage seeds stale plugin-cache content in v1 and proves selected projection starts in clean v2 state while the existing unknown-sibling guard remains fail-closed.

Codex state management and sandbox write denial consume the same shared active shadow-generation constant; regression coverage requires the sandbox profile to protect the active v2 plugin cache and not the preserved legacy v1 cache.

near_misses.failure_mode: The accepted-main Claude AGENTS artifact probe created its synthetic TMPDIR with the caller's default umask. Under a normal 022 umask the directory became 0755, so CLROOM correctly rejected session-only projection setup before the fake provider ran, making the release gate report AGENTS_BOUNDARY_SANDBOX_PROBE without exercising the intended boundary assertions.
near_misses.durable_control: The pre-tag probe explicitly chmods its synthetic TMPDIR to 0700 and fail-closes on the observed mode before launch; the provider-canary contract statically requires both the private-TMPDIR setup and its failure marker so the fixture cannot silently regress.

near_misses.failure_mode: The installed codex-app-tools bundle first exposed an ambient-path rebase defect; after that was repaired, real TUI evidence still showed codex_app failed with zero tools because the app-owned MCP requires host context that standalone CLROOM does not provide.
near_misses.durable_control: CLROOM preserves in-bundle MCP path rebasing generally, but classifies codex_app as PLUGIN_HOST_REQUIRED for standalone activation. Release qualification uses a standalone MCP fixture and requires real-provider initialize/tools-list evidence instead of server-name visibility.

near_misses.failure_mode: The MCP path-rebase repair changed `.mcp.json` bundle digest semantics. A CLROOM-owned projection left by the immediately previous candidate therefore carried a valid legacy-v1 marker digest that the repaired binary recomputed under the new semantic digest, causing the next clean launch to refuse cleanup as CLROOM_CODEX_PLUGIN_PROJECTION_CHANGED before Codex started.
near_misses.durable_control: Projection cleanup verifies ownership against either the current semantic digest or the exact legacy-v1 raw digest recorded by the existing v1 marker, but this dual-digest compatibility is cleanup-only. Runtime selected-projection verification continues to require the current semantic digest, and mutation after marker creation is still preserved and refused.

near_misses.failure_mode: mcp list --json proved only that a server declaration was visible; it could pass while the real provider later reported a failed server with zero tools.
near_misses.durable_control: Codex qualification separates configuration visibility from runtime evidence: the real pinned provider must start the selected standalone fixture and reach MCP initialize plus tools/list; the fixture must expose a real tool and pass tools/call. codex_app cannot satisfy standalone acceptance.

near_misses.failure_mode: The same candidate work was re-run on branch push and pull_request while accepted-main release readiness depended on repeated manual dispatch, increasing latency and Owner intervention without adding evidence.
near_misses.durable_control: Branch validation is pull_request-driven, push runs are main-only, superseded runs are cancelled by stable concurrency groups, and release-candidate readiness runs automatically on accepted main.

near_misses.failure_mode: The protected tag helper required the tracked v0.4.2 changelog date to equal the future annotated tagger calendar day exactly. Crossing midnight after an accepted candidate therefore forced a bookkeeping-only content mutation, new SHA, reseal and requalification even though no product or release capability changed.
near_misses.durable_control: Release Contract v1 now defines a monotonic action-time relation: the candidate carries exactly one canonical ISO changelog date and the real annotated tagger timestamp remains authoritative action-time evidence. Both local tag push and exact-tag CI call the same checker and accept declared_date <= tagger_date while rejecting future-dated declarations; checker self-tests prove same-day, later-tag and future-date-negative cases.

near_misses.failure_mode: Release-candidate readiness rejected versions that were not newer than the latest published stable release, but the canonical whole-release checker used by the protected tag path did not own that invariant. A tag path therefore depended on a prior transport having run rather than proving version progression itself.
near_misses.durable_control: check-release-contract.py now invokes the canonical lifecycle resolver against the live latest published stable tag and requires ACTIVE_CANDIDATE. The same contract also requires the candidate changelog date to be on or after the published baseline date, so version and public chronology are enforced by the tag-path authority itself.

near_misses.failure_mode: The tag helper labeled remote main/tag/ruleset/release-contract state as action-time fresh, but then performed provider pin and local provider byte checks before the irreversible push. Main or release state could therefore drift in that window and leave a protected tag pointing at a no-longer-current candidate before post-tag CI caught it.
near_misses.durable_control: Provider pin and local provider-byte checks now complete before the final remote guard. Immediately before the single tag push the helper refreshes remote main, confirms tag absence, revalidates the no-bypass tag ruleset and reruns the canonical release contract; regression coverage asserts that no provider qualification runs inside that final guard-to-push window.

near_misses.failure_mode: After the single protected tag push, reconciliation queried only the peeled ref under fail-fast shell semantics. A reconciliation read failure could therefore terminate without an explicit OUTCOME UNKNOWN state, while a concurrently created wrong-target or lightweight tag could be misreported as absent.
near_misses.durable_control: Post-push reconciliation now captures the remote query status, queries both direct and peeled tag refs, preserves local evidence on unresolved outcome, accepts success only when the peeled target equals the approved SHA, distinguishes present wrong/lightweight refs from verified absence, and reports reconciled absence only after a successful authoritative read.

near_misses.failure_mode: The accepted-main Codex pre-tag smoke created a task-owned temporary CODEX_HOME containing the standalone MCP fixture but omitted the provider-native auth fixture that CLROOM correctly requires. The first clean MCP listing therefore failed deterministically with CLROOM_CODEX_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE even though CI's real-provider qualifier already used a safe no-spend synthetic auth record.
near_misses.durable_control: The shared codex-mcp-fixture.py install path now owns a private mode-0600 no-spend synthetic Codex auth record, refuses conflicting preexisting auth state, and is consumed by both CI real-provider qualification and accepted-main/Draft plugin smokes. A pre-merge contract test requires fixture installation before the first candidate/provider launch and forbids a second hard-coded auth payload in the qualifier.

near_misses.failure_mode: The release protocol required provider/runtime/UI blockers to run on the exact PR candidate before merge, but both local plugin smokes hard-coded pretag execution to HEAD == origin/main and tag/Draft verification keyed that evidence by the accepted-main commit SHA. Squash therefore made the first full runtime rehearsal happen only after merge, allowing avoidable release escapes despite content-equivalent candidate and accepted trees.
near_misses.durable_control: Release smokes now have an exact-head rehearse mode that runs before merge and writes dynamic evidence outside the tracked tree, bound to reviewed_content_digest + exact source_tree + provider/version bytes. Tag and Draft verification accept that evidence across squash only after the current accepted tree and review digest match, while provider/mutable/action-time state is refreshed. Contract tests fail if rehearsal becomes accepted-main-only again.

near_misses.failure_mode: The exact-PR Codex rehearsal successfully completed clean/selected/clean discovery, then the PTY runtime probe unconditionally launched an additional clean CLROOM command only to recreate a shadow that already had the exact CLROOM ownership marker. That redundant fourth launch became a new blocker-producing surface and hid its root stderr.
near_misses.durable_control: The fixture now reuses an already initialized CLROOM-owned shadow when its private regular ownership marker is exact; bootstrap runs only when the marker is absent. Invalid markers fail closed, bootstrap stderr is captured for CLROOM root markers, and both fixture self-test plus provider-canary meta-contract assert the reuse/negative paths.

near_misses.failure_mode: The exact-PR Codex runtime fixture emitted a specific CODEX_MCP_FIXTURE_BLOCKED root marker, but local-codex-plugin-activation-smoke.sh routed probe-provider failures directly to the generic SELECTED_MCP_RUNTIME label. near_misses.durable_control: The outer smoke now captures probe-provider stderr, preserves the nested CODEX_MCP_FIXTURE_BLOCKED detail inside the canonical CODEX_PLUGIN_RELEASE_SMOKE_BLOCKED marker, and contract/meta-contract tests forbid collapsing that runtime root cause back to a generic marker.

near_misses.failure_mode: Provider pins and runtime qualification advanced to Codex 0.156.0 / Claude 2.1.280 while active public pages such as docs/providers.md, docs/configuration-matrix.md and SECURITY.md still described older exact provider tuples; a docs-only PR branched before the provider bump also reintroduced the stale versions into README.

Historical CHANGELOG and SECURITY version-history data stay historical, while provider claims inside SECURITY remain checked. CI never auto-rewrites docs; drift blocks the candidate until docs are corrected in-tree.

near_misses.durable_control: PRETAG_BLOCKER_CLOSURE now requires exact accepted-main staged shipping bytes and closes every technically reproducible build/package/provider/runtime/permission/API/release-policy blocker before tag. Immutable Releases is checked with the Owner-authenticated gh session before tag and pre-publish; Actions never performs that admin read. Static regression rejects post-tag build/test/provider/latest/runtime/admin checks and non-release v* workflows.

near_misses.failure_mode: The old pre-publish verifier reran check-provider-pins.sh after tag. An upstream Codex or Claude stable-tag move between tag and publication could therefore strand already-qualified immutable release bytes for reasons unrelated to those bytes.
near_misses.durable_control: Provider latest/integrity is resolved during accepted-main staging and frozen into clroom.release-stage.v1. Tag promotion and pre-publish verification validate that frozen tuple and exact bytes but never make a second mutable latest decision.

near_misses.failure_mode: CI still triggered on v* tags and reran the full target/test graph after the irreversible tag even after runtime rehearsal had been moved left, leaving an independent first-time late failure surface.

near_misses.failure_mode: The v0.4.2 escape showed that a workflow can contain a logically valid API check but still be incapable of executing it under its actual token permissions. Static permission declarations alone are insufficient proof.
near_misses.durable_control: Accepted-main attestation rehearsal uses the workflow-scoped token with actions:read to list and download the exact stage artifact and byte-compare its manifest before tag. Repository-admin policy checks are deliberately kept on the Owner-authenticated local boundary.

artifact_capability_gates.requirement: On the exact v0.4.3 PR candidate tree, pinned Codex 0.156.0 must prove the standalone-mcp@clroom-fixture whole-plugin path through real-provider MCP initialize, tools/list, a real fixture tools/call, state lifecycle closure and a final clean relaunch with no model prompt. Evidence is content-addressed to reviewed_content_digest + source_tree + provider/plugin bytes and may survive squash only after candidate-tree == accepted-tree.

On the exact v0.4.3 PR candidate tree, pinned Claude Code 2.1.280 must prove the selected skill-only plugin in a genuine local TTY with no model prompt, unchanged persistent provider config, external ancestor AGENTS exclusion and repo/nested project AGENTS retention. Evidence is content-addressed to reviewed_content_digest + source_tree + provider bytes.

The exact future v0.4.3 shipping archive built from accepted main must be provider-qualified and then exercised automatically with pinned Codex 0.156.0 through the standalone MCP initialize/tools-list/tool-call runtime boundary plus post-runtime clean closure. Stage evidence binds exact accepted source SHA/tree, reviewed_content_digest, provider/plugin bytes and shipping artifact SHA-256 with evidence_binding=exact-release-artifact-v1.

Before tag, the exact future v0.4.3 shipping archive from accepted main must pass the local Claude 2.1.280 skill-only selected-plugin TTY proof, including project AGENTS retention/external ancestor exclusion and no model prompt. Stage evidence must bind the exact accepted source SHA/tree, reviewed_content_digest, Claude provider bytes and shipping artifact SHA-256 with evidence_binding=exact-release-artifact-v1.

After the protected tag, automation may only resolve the already accepted exact stage, create tag-bound provenance/SBOM attestations, create/update a Draft, upload the accepted payload bytes and download/cmp-reconcile the exact six assets. No build/test/provider/runtime/latest/admin-policy gate may first execute here.

product_outcome: Ship v0.4.3 from the published v0.4.0 baseline with the bounded Codex/Claude whole-plugin capability accumulated in the unpublished v0.4.1/v0.4.2 candidates, while repairing the release harness after the second avoidable late escape. The release train now closes all technically reproducible build/package/provider/runtime/permission/release-policy blockers before a protected tag: exact PR rehearsal remains pre-merge, accepted main builds and qualifies the exact future shipping bytes once, provider registry freshness/integrity is frozen into a staged manifest, Codex whole-plugin runtime and attestation mechanism are rehearsed on those staged bytes, and Claude performs the one genuine local human-TTY stage proof against the same archive. The tag workflow is promotion-only and can only add unavoidable tag-bound attestations, create the Draft, upload the already accepted bytes and byte-reconcile them. Pre-publish verification rechecks immutable release policy, tag/Draft identity, exact staged-byte equality, attestations and promotion success without rebuilding, rerunning providers, or reopening a mutable provider-latest decision.

contract_evolution_review.rationale: The v0.4.2 protected tag exposed the second avoidable late release escape in the v0.4.x train. Product/provider runtime had already been rehearsed, but the release architecture still allowed new blocker-producing surfaces after tag: full CI, fresh shipping build/qualification, mutable provider-latest rechecks, Draft runtime, and a repository-admin Immutable Releases API check executed under an Actions token that could not read it. The repair therefore addresses the class, not the marker: exact future shipping bytes are staged and fully qualified before tag; provider freshness is frozen at staging; Actions token capabilities used for promotion are rehearsed before tag; repository-admin policy is owned by the Owner-authenticated local boundary; tag automation is promotion-only; and static negative controls forbid reintroducing first-time post-tag blockers.
